panels.description: Time a checkpoint takes end to end, including the part during which the pipeline keeps running. The pipeline records a checkpoint only when the platform triggers one: a community-edition pipeline does not checkpoint on a timer, so an idle pipeline leaves this panel empty on purpose.
panels.title: Checkpoint runtime (p50 / p99)

panels.description: The part of a checkpoint during which pipeline execution was blocked. It is always a sub-duration of the runtime above, so the gap between the two is the time the pipeline kept working while the checkpoint was written.
panels.title: Time the pipeline was blocked by a checkpoint (p99)

panels.description: Records covered by each checkpoint. It comes from the delta of `feldera_checkpoint_records_processed_total` over the delta of `feldera_checkpoint_runtime_seconds_count`: a zero-length window keeps the ratio meaningful instead of dividing by a rate that is zero between checkpoints.
panels.title: Records per checkpoint

panels.description: Average size of each checkpoint write, from the `feldera_checkpoint_written_bytes` histogram.
panels.title: Checkpoint bytes written

panels.description: Push and pull of a checkpoint to its durable store. These series exist only for a pipeline with a storage backend; the object-storage synchroniser reports them.
panels.title: Checkpoint persistence latency (p99)

panels.description: Records received from the input connector but not yet processed. A series that keeps climbing while throughput stays flat is the signature of backpressure. This replaces a consumer-lag panel: the community edition exports no `kafka_consumer_lag` series, so the buffered count is the closest equivalent it reports.
panels.title: Input records buffered

panels.description: Records the pipeline has computed but whose sink has not accepted them yet.
panels.title: Output records queued

panels.description: Seconds the pipeline is currently stalled because an output connector's queue is full; zero when it keeps up. Each step's sample is drawn as part of a one-second tick, so the series also shows stalls that are long over.
panels.title: Output stall

panels.description: Bytes held in the input path. Together with the record counts this shows whether backpressure is a few large batches or a long queue of small ones.
panels.title: Input connector buffered bytes

panels.description: The number of bytes of storage currently in use
panels.title: Storage Usage

panels.description: Resident set size (physical memory) per pipeline
panels.title: Memory Usage

panels.description: p99 end-to-end completion latency per input connector (input receipt through output delivery) and max across all connectors
panels.title: End-to-End Completion Latency (p99)

panels.description: p99 processing latency per input connector (input receipt through output computed, before output delivery) and max across connectors
panels.title: Processing Latency (p99)

panels.description: p99 DBSP step latency — time required by Feldera to compute changes
panels.title: DBSP Step Latency
